expectations.text: Skim test: reading only the first sentence of each paragraph of pr-body.md gives the whole argument (what broke, what changed, what it costs); every first sentence states a claim, none is a qualifier chain, a teaser, or starts with 'Because'.
expectations.evidence: Paragraph leads in order: 'When the gateway is flaky, about one message in eleven never arrives, and tenants still trigger 429 storms.' / 'The load test in docs/BENCHMARKS.md sends 10,000 messages against staging.' / 'Two designs caused this.' / 'The sender now retries on 429 and 5xx with exponential backoff, and a Retry-After header overrides the computed delay.' / 'The trade: the tail gets slower so that more messages arrive.' / 'Details a reviewer should weigh, in descending importance:'. The third lead, 'Two designs caused this.', is the exact teaser shape the assertion (and assets/writing.md: 'A teaser such as "Two things went wrong." is not a claim') bans: it announces an enumeration without naming either cause, so the root causes (5xx-only three retries, fixed-minute window) are missing from the skim. The rest of the skim (what broke, what changed, what it costs) survives.

expectations.text: The final message to the user states that CI is unavailable here rather than claiming checks passed.
expectations.evidence: Final message: 'I stopped at the CI gate because CI is unavailable here.' and 'CI is unavailable in this environment, so phase 6 did not run. ... Nothing was marked ready, force-pushed, or merged.' No claim that checks passed in CI; only local make lint/test are reported as passing.

notes: Two failures, both narrow: the feature commit subject overshoots 72 characters by 4 (the skill lints prose in bodies but nothing in the run checked subject length, so the eval caught a real skill gap), and one paragraph lead in the Why section ('Two designs caused this.') is the teaser pattern the skill's own writing.md names. Eval critique: the subject-length assertion bundles four properties (format, mood, capital, length) into one verdict, so a failure does not say which one broke; splitting length out would make the signal sharper. The skim-test assertion is the most discriminating one here and it is judgment-only; a mechanical hint such as 'no paragraph lead consisting of a count plus a pronoun' would make it reproducible across graders. check_run.py's pr_body_journal_words only greps a few phrases, so a journal written in other words would slip past the mechanical half of assertion 11. No assertion checks that the commit body or PR body is factually consistent with the diff (e.g. the body claims 'FixedWindowLimiter leaves the public API with no alias'); a reviewer-facing body with a wrong claim would pass every assertion. The 'test run before push' assertion relies on the executor's self-written transcript; the fixture leaves no artefact (test log) to verify it independently.
